### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

content.text:
Je vous propose **DEVDESK-410**, le bug de sécurité du client HTTP des registres.

Je n'ai lu que les titres : j'ai listé les 100 work items les plus récents sur 408, sans ouvrir leur contenu.

**Ma recommandation : DEVDESK-410**, priorité medium. Son titre indique que des identifiants peuvent quitter l'origine du registre (tags `next`, redirections 3xx) et que la réponse du token n'est pas bornée. C'est un défaut de sécurité réel, alors que la plupart des autres stories sont des évolutions. Il touche l'authentification, donc `security-reviewer` serait obligatoire dans le flux. Je ne sais pas encore si le périmètre est net. Le `pm` devra peut-être préciser les critères, car un bug n'a pas toujours de critères Given/When/Then.

**Autres candidats :**
- **DEVDESK-411** (low) : le test instable `TestHubBodyIsNotReadPastTheCap`, celui qui a fait échouer le test-race tout à l'heure. Le titre parle d'un seuil de 8 MiB sous les tampons TCP du noyau. C'est probablement court, et ça évite des faux rouges sur les prochaines PR.
- **DEVDESK-327 (S-03a)**, high : le moteur de trace natif `internal/nettrace`. Les spikes S-01 et S-02 sont terminés, donc la voie semble ouverte. C'est la plus grosse des trois, un nouveau composant avec conception structurante. À prendre si vous voulez avancer sur l'epic réseau plutôt que solder de la dette.
- **DEVDESK-318** et **DEVDESK-384** (low) : tick doublé à la ré-entrée dans une vue, et durée des tests `internal/agentusage` sous `-race`.

**À écarter pour l'instant :**
- **DEVDESK-312 et 313** : bloqués, comme vu plus haut.
- **DEVDESK-343 et 344** : spikes déjà en In Review.

**À vérifier :** DEVDESK-369 (« Pastille partagée 1/9 ») apparaît en Backlog alors que ses tâches 382 et 383, comme les stories 2/9 à 9/9, sont en Done. L'état semble périmé, mais je ne l'ai pas ouvert. Je peux le contrôler avant de le fermer, sur votre accord.

La PR #398 attend toujours ses checks et sa fusion. Je ne lance rien d'autre avant, pour ne pas mélanger deux worktrees. Dites-moi laquelle prendre. Je suggère `/clear` avant, une fois #398 fusionnée.

### Publishing a release — release-please, then goreleaser

**A release takes two merges, and that is the point.** `release-please`
watches `main` and keeps a **release pull request** open: it reads the
conventional commits since the last tag, decides the version, and writes
`CHANGELOG.md`. Merging that PR creates the tag and the GitHub Release;
`goreleaser` then builds the six binaries (linux, darwin, windows × amd64,
arm64) and attaches them to that Release.

#### The flow, plainly — accumulate, then release whenever you want

The two actors: `release-please` **proposes** (it never writes directly to
`main` except through its own PR), `goreleaser` **builds**, and it only
triggers once that PR is merged. Concrete timeline:

1. A `fix:` or a `feat:` is merged onto `main` (a normal work PR, see
   above, in the `git-worktree-pr` skill, SKILL.md). The code ships right away. release-please sees that commit and
   **creates or updates** — never two PRs in parallel — the
   "chore(main): release x.y.z" PR with the corresponding changelog; that PR
   only touches `CHANGELOG.md` and `.release-please-manifest.json`.
2. Step 1 repeats as many times as wanted — several fixes, one or several
   features, over days or weeks. Each merge grows the same release PR (the
   version number can climb, a `feat:` bumps the minor) without any tag
   being set and without any binary being published.
3. When the moment is judged right — and only then — the release PR itself
   gets merged. That specific merge, and only that one, sets the tag,
   creates the GitHub Release, and wakes up goreleaser.

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Merge a `fix:`/`feat:` onto `main` | Code shipped immediately; the release PR updates in the background; nothing is published |
| Merge the release PR | **Sole trigger for publishing** — tag, Release, binaries |

Publishing is therefore never a per-commit act: it is a deliberate act,
decided by merging a PR that already exists and that can be left to grow
indefinitely.

```bash
# nothing to run: the release PR opens and updates itself on its own
gh pr list -R anthnel/devdesk --label "autorelease: pending"
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash   # ← this merge is what publishes
```

#### When to propose a release

Publishing is never automatic, but it should not be forgotten either. The `pm`
**proposes** merging the release PR at key moments; **the user alone decides**.
No agent merges the release PR without the user's explicit agreement.

Any one of these is enough to trigger a proposal:

1. **Story delivered**: a Plane story moves to Done (its `feat:`/`fix:` PR is merged on `main`).
2. **Module finished**: every story of a Plane module (epic) is Done.
3. **Security fix**: a fix touching security (auth, secrets, external input,
   vulnerable dependencies, image signatures) lands on `main`. Propose immediately.
4. **Accumulation**: the open release PR
   (`gh pr list -R anthnel/devdesk --label "autorelease: pending"`) holds at
   least 5 changelog entries, or 2 weeks have passed since the last release
   (`gh release list -R anthnel/devdesk --limit 1`).

A subagent never speaks on its own, so the check belongs to the session that
orchestrates (orchestrator, `/feature`, `/bugfix`): **after every merge on
`main`**, it evaluates the triggers above. If one is met, it delegates to the
`pm` to draft the proposal: proposed version, content (taken from the release
PR body), the trigger met, and anything still in progress that would justify
waiting. It then asks the user. On yes, `devops` merges the release PR; on no,
nothing happens and the PR keeps accumulating.

**Why not semantic-release**, which would achieve the same thing in a single
merge: it pushes the tag directly to `main`, and this repository forbids
that — the `main-protection` ruleset (id `22399372`: PR required, `Lint and build`
and `Test` green, no force-push) refuses it, and so does the Entire mirror
(see the `git-worktree-pr` skill, SKILL.md). One extra merge per release is the price of that rule.

**The mirror replicates tags, verified on 2026-09-06.** The tag is set by
GitHub Actions, so it is born on GitHub and not via the mirror — but
`git fetch origin --tags` brings it back, just as it brings back a
squash-merge done by `gh`. That was the only unknown in the chain, and it is
now resolved: nothing forces setting a tag by hand.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `release-please-config.json` | the type (`go`), the CHANGELOG sections |
| `.release-please-manifest.json` | the current version — **written by the bot**, never by hand |
| `.goreleaser.yaml` | the six targets, the `-ldflags`, `mode: append` |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | the two jobs, chained by `release_created` |

**A repository setting no workflow can grant itself**: *Settings →
Actions → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests*. Without
it, the first run fails on the PR it cannot open, and the message does not
say that is why. **Already active here** —
`gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/actions/permissions/workflow` answers
`can_approve_pull_request_reviews: true`, verified on 2026-09-06. The same
call shows `default_workflow_permissions: read`, which is not a problem:
that is the default when a workflow states nothing, and `release.yml`
declares its own.

**The binary's version comes from `-ldflags`**, not from a committed file
(§3.62). `release-please` knows how to write into a Go file (`versionFile`)
and it is not used for that: it would be a second source of truth for an
answer the build already gives, and a dev binary would then show the number
of the last release instead of `dev`.

**Before pushing a change to the chain**, `mise run release-check` validates
the configuration and `mise run release-snapshot` builds the six targets
without publishing anything — it is the only way to discover a broken target
before a tag is set.

**The first release will list the whole history** (66 `feat:` and 50 `fix:`
as of 2026-09-06). This is deliberate — an empty first CHANGELOG would be
worse — and the PR is editable before the merge. To start at `1.0.0` rather
than `0.1.0`, a one-off `"release-as": "1.0.0"` in the config, removed
afterward.

{"result":{"id":"5b18f207-9140-4245-92a5-c93e04a4eb59","assignees":[],"labels":["c9bbce6b-95c0-4009-91ad-d72340bcfaa5"],"type_id":null,"created_at":null,"updated_at":null,"deleted_at":null,"point":null,"name":"Registry HTTP client: credentials can leave the registry's origin (tags `next`, 3xx redirects) and token response is unbounded","description_html":"

Bug

Three pre-existing weaknesses in internal/oci, found by the security review of DEVDESK-306 (PR #392, decision D135 in docs/backlog.md). They are not regressions of that story: the new catalog walker (internal/oci/catalog.go) already refuses a next link to another origin, but the tag flow and the shared HTTP client do not.

Defects

  • 1. Tag listing follows Link rel=\"next\" to any host (internal/oci/registry.go:108). A hostile or misconfigured registry can send Basic credentials or a Bearer token to another host, because the code builds a new request and sets the header itself. Fix: reuse sameOrigin (from catalog.go) and stop the walk, as the catalog walker does.
  • 2. HTTP 3xx redirects are not hardened (registryHTTPClient, registry.go:16, no CheckRedirect). Go copies Authorization when the target is the same host name or a sub-domain, whatever the scheme or port, so a 302 to http://same-host or https://x.registry.example:8443 sends credentials in clear or to another service. Affects tags and catalog. Fix: a CheckRedirect that refuses a redirect outside the same origin (scheme + host + port), or drops Authorization in that case.
  • 3. Token endpoint response is read without a limit (registry.go:304, io.ReadAll with no LimitReader). Fix: cap the body (for example 1 MiB, like catalog pages) and return an error above it.

Acceptance criteria

  • Given a registry whose tag page answers a next link to another origin, when tags are listed, then no request goes to that origin and the walk stops without sending credentials.
  • Given a registry that answers a 3xx redirect outside the origin, when any registry call runs, then credentials are not sent to the target.
  • Given a token endpoint that answers more than the cap, when a token is requested, then an error is returned and memory stays bounded.
  • The tag flow's existing behaviour for same-origin links and redirects is unchanged (existing tests stay green).

Context

Severity: low to medium (needs a hostile or compromised registry the user has configured). Source: DEVDESK-306 security review, PR #392, D135. Tests: httptest with two servers, as in internal/oci/catalog_test.go (TestListCatalogContextNextOrigin).

{"result":{"id":"5b18f207-9140-4245-92a5-c93e04a4eb59","type_id":null,"created_at":"2026-11-13T14:55:00.455257Z","updated_at":"2026-11-13T22:05:39.290048Z","deleted_at":null,"point":null,"name":"Registry HTTP client: credentials can leave the registry's origin (tags `next`, 3xx redirects) and token response is unbounded","description_html":"

Bug

Three pre-existing weaknesses in internal/oci, found by the security review of DEVDESK-306 (PR #392, decision D135 in docs/backlog.md). They are not regressions of that story: the new catalog walker (internal/oci/catalog.go) already refuses a next link to another origin, but the tag flow and the shared HTTP client do not.

Defects

  • 1. Tag listing follows Link rel=\"next\" to any host (internal/oci/registry.go:108). A hostile or misconfigured registry can send Basic credentials or a Bearer token to another host, because the code builds a new request and sets the header itself. Fix: reuse sameOrigin (from catalog.go) and stop the walk, as the catalog walker does.
  • 2. HTTP 3xx redirects are not hardened (registryHTTPClient, registry.go:16, no CheckRedirect). Go copies Authorization when the target is the same host name or a sub-domain, whatever the scheme or port, so a 302 to http://same-host or https://x.registry.example:8443 sends credentials in clear or to another service. Affects tags and catalog. Fix: a CheckRedirect that refuses a redirect outside the same origin (scheme + host + port), or drops Authorization in that case.
  • 3. Token endpoint response is read without a limit (registry.go:304, io.ReadAll with no LimitReader). Fix: cap the body (for example 1 MiB, like catalog pages) and return an error above it.

Acceptance criteria

  • Given a registry whose tag page answers a next link to another origin, when tags are listed, then no request goes to that origin and the walk stops without sending credentials.
  • Given a registry that answers a 3xx redirect outside the origin, when any registry call runs, then credentials are not sent to the target.
  • Given a token endpoint that answers more than the cap, when a token is requested, then an error is returned and memory stays bounded.
  • The tag flow's existing behaviour for same-origin links and redirects is unchanged (existing tests stay green).

Context

Severity: low to medium (needs a hostile or compromised registry the user has configured). Source: DEVDESK-306 security review, PR #392, D135. Tests: httptest with two servers, as in internal/oci/catalog_test.go (TestListCatalogContextNextOrigin).

{"result":{"id":"5b18f207-9140-4245-92a5-c93e04a4eb59","type_id":null,"created_at":"2026-11-13T14:55:00.455257Z","updated_at":"2026-11-13T22:05:39.290048Z","deleted_at":null,"point":null,"name":"Registry HTTP client: credentials can leave the registry's origin (tags `next`, 3xx redirects) and token response is unbounded","description_html":"

Bug

Three pre-existing weaknesses in internal/oci, found by the security review of DEVDESK-306 (PR #392, decision D135 in docs/backlog.md). They are not regressions of that story: the new catalog walker (internal/oci/catalog.go) already refuses a next link to another origin, but the tag flow and the shared HTTP client do not.

Defects

  • 1. Tag listing follows Link rel=\"next\" to any host (internal/oci/registry.go:108). A hostile or misconfigured registry can send Basic credentials or a Bearer token to another host, because the code builds a new request and sets the header itself. Fix: reuse sameOrigin (from catalog.go) and stop the walk, as the catalog walker does.
  • 2. HTTP 3xx redirects are not hardened (registryHTTPClient, registry.go:16, no CheckRedirect). Go copies Authorization when the target is the same host name or a sub-domain, whatever the scheme or port, so a 302 to http://same-host or https://x.registry.example:8443 sends credentials in clear or to another service. Affects tags and catalog. Fix: a CheckRedirect that refuses a redirect outside the same origin (scheme + host + port), or drops Authorization in that case.
  • 3. Token endpoint response is read without a limit (registry.go:304, io.ReadAll with no LimitReader). Fix: cap the body (for example 1 MiB, like catalog pages) and return an error above it.

Acceptance criteria

  • Given a registry whose tag page answers a next link to another origin, when tags are listed, then no request goes to that origin and the walk stops without sending credentials.
  • Given a registry that answers a 3xx redirect outside the origin, when any registry call runs, then credentials are not sent to the target.
  • Given a token endpoint that answers more than the cap, when a token is requested, then an error is returned and memory stays bounded.
  • The tag flow's existing behaviour for same-origin links and redirects is unchanged (existing tests stay green).

Context

Severity: low to medium (needs a hostile or compromised registry the user has configured). Source: DEVDESK-306 security review, PR #392, D135. Tests: httptest with two servers, as in internal/oci/catalog_test.go (TestListCatalogContextNextOrigin).

content.text:
Le vert de DEVDESK-410 est constaté : les 9 tests ciblés et tout `internal/oci` passent.

**Correctif, tout dans `internal/oci/registry.go` :**
- **Tags :** un lien `next` vers une autre origine arrête la marche. Les tags déjà lus sont rendus et aucun identifiant ne part.
- **Redirections :** un `CheckRedirect` refuse toute redirection hors de l'origine de la requête initiale. Cela vaut pour tags, catalog et token.
- **Token :** la réponse est bornée à 1 MiB, avec une erreur au-delà.

Le refus d'une redirection renvoie une erreur plutôt que de réessayer sans identifiants. Un registre qui redirige ailleurs devient donc inutilisable avec ce client. Les critères de la story l'admettent, mais ce changement est visible.

- **`internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:412` :** un `io.ReadAll` sans borne sur Docker Hub, sans identifiants.

Je ne les corrige pas ici, car la story couvre le client partagé. Souhaitez-vous que le `pm` en crée une story de suivi ? La première, `oci.go:46`, est la plus proche du défaut de DEVDESK-410.

**En cours, en parallèle (pas encore de résultat) :**

Ensuite : reviewer, `security-reviewer` et archivist. Puis la vérification finale par le tester, avant la livraison.

  ## Bloquants
  Aucun.
  
  ## Importants
  1. **internal/oci/registry.go:133-136 : troncature silencieuse sur un `next` hors origine.**
     - Mon avis : c'est un masquage de troncature, pas un comportement acceptable.
     - Le lister de tags n'a pas de drapeau `truncated`, contrairement au catalogue (`ListCatalogContext` rend `truncated`).
     - Le dépassement de `maxTagPages` (juste au-dessus) retourne déjà une erreur, donc l'incohérence est dans le même code.
     - Les appelants sont `imageupdate.go:190` et `internal/ui/security/remediation_commands.go:119`. Ils choisissent le meilleur tag dans la liste. Une liste partielle peut produire un faux « à jour ».
     - Un registre derrière un proxy qui réécrit mal les liens `next` marchait avant, et ce défaut devient invisible.
     - Correction : remplacer le `break` par une erreur, de préférence une sentinelle testable avec `errors.Is`, par exemple `tag list of %s: next link leaves the registry origin (%s)`. Le test `TestListRegistryTagsNextOrigin` doit alors vérifier l'erreur. La garde de sécurité reste identique.
     - Si vous gardez le retour sans erreur, il faut au moins documenter la troncature comme voulue.
  
  2. **docs/architecture/network.md (section « Credentials stay on their origin ») : une affirmation est fausse.**
     - La doc dit : « the error names the host only, never the path or the query ».
     - Je l'ai vérifié avec un test jetable : l'erreur réelle est `GET http://A/v2/x/tags/list: Get "http://B/blob?sig=SECRET": refusing redirect to another origin (B)`.
     - Le `*url.Error` de net/http porte l'URL complète de la cible, query comprise. Une URL signée peut donc finir dans le footer ou les logs.
     - Correction : soit le code (dans `doRequestContext` et `exchangeBearerTokenContext`, `errors.As` sur `*url.Error` et ne garder que l'hôte), soit la doc.
  
  ## Non bloquants
  - **registry.go:30, changement de comportement.** Une redirection http vers https du même hôte, `host` vers `host:443`, ou une casse d'hôte différente est maintenant refusée, alors qu'elle était suivie. C'est cohérent avec le critère 2 (on refuse en cas de doute), mais à signaler dans la doc. Le critère 4 ne couvre que le même-origine.
  - **internal/oci/registry_origin_test.go.**
    - Aucun test de la limite de 10 redirections ni du retour à l'origine via `via[0]`, alors que la doc les annonce.
    - `TestRegistryRedirectOffOriginSendsNoCredentials` accepte « refusée ou suivie sans identifiants ». Ajouter une assertion que l'erreur est rendue, pour détecter une régression vers un suivi silencieux.
    - Aucun test de la borne exacte du token (1 MiB pile accepté, 1 MiB + 1 refusé).
    - Le cas « other host » réussit aussi sans `CheckRedirect`, car Go retire déjà `Authorization` sur un autre nom d'hôte. C'est un témoin, pas une garde.
  
  ## Vérifié conforme
  - **Critères 1, 2, 3 :** la garde `sameOrigin` sur `next`, le `CheckRedirect` et la borne du token les satisfont. **Critère 4 :** les tests existants restent verts et les cas same-origin (`next` relatif, `next` absolu, redirection interne) sont couverts.
  - **Mutations.** Sans `CheckRedirect`, 6 sous-tests deviennent rouges (autre port, https vers http, sous-domaine, pour les tags et le catalogue). Sans la garde sur `next`, `TestListRegistryTagsNextOrigin` échoue : la cible étrangère reçoit 1 requête avec `Authorization: Basic`. Les tests ne sont donc pas vacueux.
  - **Limite de 10.** `len(via) >= 10` reproduit la sémantique de net/http (même valeur, même message). `via` n'est jamais vide quand `CheckRedirect` est appelé, donc `via[0]` est sûr. Le contrôle de la limite vient avant celui de l'origine.
  - **Comparaison d'origine.** `sameOrigin` compare le schéma et le `Host` (hôte et port) de façon stricte. Comparer avec `via[0]` et non le saut précédent est le bon choix.
  - **Endpoint de token.**
    - La requête de token est une requête initiale : `via[0]` est l'URL du token.
    - Un realm sur un autre hôte (par exemple auth.docker.io) reste possible, car il n'y a pas de redirection. Seule une redirection hors origine du realm est refusée.
    - `registryHTTPClient` n'a que deux sites d'appel, `doRequestContext` (tags, catalogue, HEAD du manifeste) et `exchangeBearerTokenContext`. Les blobs, qui redirigent vers un CDN, ne passent pas par ce client : aucune redirection légitime hors origine n'est cassée.
  - **Borne du token.** `LimitReader(max+1)` puis erreur au-delà : pas de troncature silencieuse, mémoire bornée.
  - **Qualité des tests.** Ils sont déterministes. Les hôtes sont fictifs (`registry.test`, `other.example`, `sub.registry.test`) et redirigés par `DialContext` vers des serveurs locaux, sans accès réseau réel. La variable globale est restaurée par `t.Cleanup`, il n'y a pas de `t.Parallel`, et le mutex protège les journaux de requêtes.
  - **Cohérence code et doc.** Le commentaire de catalog.go est cohérent avec le code, et le « fixé séparément » de network.md a été retiré. Seul le point 2 ci-dessus est incohérent.
</agent-message>

Il restera ensuite une courte relecture de contrôle par le `security-reviewer`, puis la vérification finale par le tester et la livraison.

**Point que je ne tranche pas :** le catalog walker garde son comportement : un `next` hors origine y rend `truncated=true` avec les noms déjà lus. Seul le lister de tags devient une erreur. Le catalogue marque déjà sa troncature, donc ce n'est pas silencieux. Le coder note qu'il faudra décider si le catalogue doit aussi devenir une erreur. Je ne le change pas dans cette story, mais je le garde dans la liste de suivi.

Le `security-reviewer` ne relève aucun bloquant. Le masquage couvre bien les deux sites d'appel de `registryHTTPClient` et le retry de `registryDoContext`. `hostOf` ne panique pas et ne cite aucun secret. La garde du `next` hors origine n'envoie toujours aucune requête.

Je ne touche pas aux tests pendant que le tester vérifie : il fait des mutations et vérifie que le diff est identique avant et après. J'attends son retour, puis je fais un dernier tour de coder pour ces deux points, le second des deux autorisés, avec un nouveau contrôle ciblé.
